title: The Iran war, explained: eight months that remade West Asia
ticker: The Iran war explained: from the first strike on 28 February to the fight for the Strait of Hormuz

scenes.title: The war that remade West Asia
scenes.say: A supreme leader killed. The world's most important oil route choked. And a region still on the edge. This is the Iran war, from the first strike to today.

scenes.title: Years of rising tension
scenes.say: The road to war was long. In 2018 the US walked out of the nuclear deal. In June 2025, Israel and Iran fought the 12-Day War. Then Iran's currency collapsed, and protests swept the country.
scenes.speak: The road to war was long. In twenty eighteen the US walked out of the nuclear deal. In June twenty twenty-five, Israel and Iran fought the twelve-day war. Then Iran's currency collapsed, and protests swept the country.

scenes.title: Protest, and a crackdown

photos.caption: Protesters in the street at night
A protester beside a street fire

scenes.say: On 8 January, security forces opened fire. Officials in Iran's own health ministry put the dead at 30,000 or more. The US then began its biggest military build-up in the region since the 2003 Iraq war.
scenes.speak: On the eighth of January, security forces opened fire. Officials in Iran's own health ministry put the dead at thirty thousand or more. The US then began its biggest military build-up in the region since the two thousand three Iraq war.

scenes.label: US and Israeli strikes in the first 12 hours
scenes.say: On 28 February, the US and Israel struck. Nearly 900 strikes in the first 12 hours, on missiles, air defences and Iran's leadership.
scenes.speak: On the twenty-eighth of February, the US and Israel struck. Nearly nine hundred strikes in the first twelve hours, on missiles, air defences and Iran's leadership.

scenes.title: Tehran under fire
scenes.say: The first wave killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and dozens of top officials. It also hit a girls' school near Bandar Abbas, killing about 170 people.

scenes.title: A harder line takes over
scenes.say: But the regime didn't collapse. It hardened. His son Mojtaba Khamenei, seen as even more hawkish, became supreme leader. And the Revolutionary Guards took control of wartime decisions.

scenes.title: A war across the region
scenes.say: Iran answered with hundreds of missiles and thousands of drones, at Israel and at US bases and embassies across the Gulf, from Iraq and Jordan to Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE. The aim: make the war too costly to continue.

scenes.title: A region frozen
items: Dubai airport hit on day two
Shipping rerouted from Hormuz and the Red Sea
Houthis open a front from Yemen
scenes.say: On day two, drones hit Dubai airport, one of the world's busiest. Flights across the region stopped. Ships avoided both Hormuz and the Red Sea, and in late March the Houthis in Yemen opened another front.

scenes.title: The chokepoint: Hormuz
scenes.say: Then the real battle began: the Strait of Hormuz, the channel for a fifth of the world's oil. Traffic fell by more than 90 per cent.
scenes.speak: Then the real battle began: the Strait of Hormuz, the channel for a fifth of the world's oil. Traffic fell by more than ninety per cent.

scenes.title: Asia felt it first
scenes.say: Oil jumped from about 70 dollars a barrel to an average of 103 in March. Parts of Asia faced fuel shortages and rationing. India, which buys much of its crude from the Gulf, felt the squeeze.
scenes.speak: Oil jumped from about seventy dollars a barrel to an average of a hundred and three in March. Parts of Asia faced fuel shortages and rationing. India, which buys much of its crude from the Gulf, felt the squeeze.

scenes.label: people displaced in Lebanon by late March
scenes.say: On 2 March, Hezbollah joined in from Lebanon. Israel invaded the south, and by late March more than 11 lakh people had fled their homes.
scenes.speak: On the second of March, Hezbollah joined in from Lebanon. Israel invaded the south, and by late March more than eleven lakh people had fled their homes.

scenes.text: A whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again.
scenes.say: By April, Trump set a deadline and posted that a whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again. Hours later, he agreed to a ceasefire.

scenes.title: Iran's toll plan
scenes.say: Through the spring, Iran let some ships through, on its own routes, and for a hefty toll. In May it even set up an authority to run the strait. Washington answered with a naval blockade of Iran's ports.

scenes.title: Talks, a deal, then collapse

items.what: A memorandum to end the war

scenes.say: Pakistan brokered the ceasefire. Talks in Islamabad failed, and the US blockaded Iran's ports. In June came a deal meant to end the war. But in July Iran struck three ships, and Trump declared the truce over.
scenes.speak: Pakistan brokered the ceasefire. Talks in Islamabad failed, and the US blockaded Iran's ports. In June came a deal meant to end the war. But in July Iran struck three ships, and Trump declared the truce over.

scenes.label: US strikes on about 140 targets in a single week
scenes.say: The fighting came back hard. In one week of July, US forces carried out more than 300 strikes on about 140 targets. Two American soldiers were killed in Jordan, and Iran suspended the June deal.
scenes.speak: The fighting came back hard. In one week of July, US forces carried out more than three hundred strikes on about a hundred and forty targets. Two American soldiers were killed in Jordan, and Iran suspended the June deal.

scenes.title: Thousands dead, millions displaced
scenes.source: Lebanese and Iranian health ministries; Israeli figures; Pentagon
scenes.say: The toll, by official counts: more than 4,000 dead in Lebanon, nearly 3,500 in Iran, dozens in Israel and the Gulf, and 21 American troops. The true figures are likely higher.
scenes.speak: The toll, by official counts: more than four thousand dead in Lebanon, nearly three and a half thousand in Iran, dozens in Israel and the Gulf, and twenty-one American troops. The true figures are likely higher.

scenes.title: October: a tense standoff
items: US says it has cleared Iran's mines from shipping lanes
Gulf oil exports back to prewar levels
Regional envoys press Tehran to avoid a new war
scenes.say: Now, the US says it has cleared Iran's mines, and Gulf oil exports are back to prewar levels. But tankers are still being hit, and Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish envoys are in Tehran trying to stop a new round of war.

scenes.title: War, or a deal?
scenes.say: With elections in Israel and the US days away, the threats are getting louder. For India, the question is simple: will the oil keep flowing through Hormuz?
